To determine the correct antibiotic for selection, we need to identify the antibiotic resistance genes present in the plasmids used in the Golden Gate cloning reaction. Golden Gate cloning typically involves assembling multiple DNA fragments into a destination vector. The resulting construct will contain the resistance marker(s) of the backbone vector and potentially any markers from the insert fragments, depending on the design. However, standard practice is that the final plasmid must confer resistance to at least one antibiotic to allow for selection of transformants.
